questions.q: What have the psalmists heard with their ears?
questions.a: They have heard what work God did in their days, in the days of old.

questions.q: What did God do with his hand?
questions.a: God drove out the nations with his hand and planted the people of Israel.

questions.q: How did the Israelites obtain the land?
questions.a: They did not obtain the land by their own sword or by their own arm, but by God’s right hand because he favored them.

questions.q: What do the Israelites do through God?
questions.a: Through God they defeat their enemies, and through God’s name they trample those who rise up against them.

questions.q: In what does the psalmist not trust?
questions.a: He does not trust in his bow, and his sword does not save him.

questions.q: From what does God save them?
questions.a: God saves them from their enemies and shames those who hate them.
God has rejected and humiliated them and no longer goes out with their armies.

questions.q: What does God make the Israelites do?
questions.a: God makes them turn back from the adversary.

questions.q: What do those who hate the Israelites do?
questions.a: Those who hate them take spoil for themselves.

questions.q: What has God made the Israelites like?
questions.a: God has made them like sheep destined for slaughter and has scattered them as slaves among the nations.

questions.q: What has God made the Israelites to their neighbors?
questions.a: God has made them a reproach to their neighbors, a scorn and a derision to those around them.

questions.q: Why is the psalmist’s dishonor before him all the day long?
questions.a: His dishonor is before him, and the shame of his face has covered him because of the voice of him who rebukes and insults, because of the enemy and the avenger.

questions.q: What have the Israelites not done?
questions.a: They have not forgotten God nor dealt falsely with God’s covenant.

questions.q: What have the Israelites’ heart and steps not done?
questions.a: Their heart has not turned back, nor have their steps turned aside from God’s way.

questions.q: What has God done to them?
questions.a: God has allowed their enemies to ruin their land as if darkness has covered it.
God would discover whether they had forgotten the name of their God or spread out their hands to a foreign god.

questions.q: What are the Israelites considered to be because of God?
questions.a: They are considered to be like sheep for slaughter.

questions.q: What has happened to the Israelites?
questions.a: They are helpless as if they had fallen down and could not get up.

questions.q: What does the psalmist pray that God would do?
questions.a: He prays that God might rise up for their help and redeem them for the sake of God’s covenant faithfulness.

commentary.text: A petition for succour and relief.

Former experiences of God's power and goodness are strong supports to faith, and powerful pleas in prayer under present calamities. The many victories Israel obtained, were not by their own strength or merit, but by God's favour and free grace. The less praise this allows us, the more comfort it affords, that we may see all as coming from the favour of God. He fought for Israel, else they had fought in vain. This is applicable to the planting of the Christian church in the world, which was not by any human policy or power. Christ, by his Spirit, went forth conquering and to conquer; and he that planted a church for himself in the world, will support it by the same power and goodness. They trusted and triumphed in and through him. Let him that glories, glory in the Lord. But if they have the comfort of his name, let them give unto him the glory due unto it.

The believer must have times of temptation, affliction, and discouragement; the church must have seasons of persecution. At such times the people of God will be ready to fear that he has cast them off, and that his name and truth will be dishonoured. But they should look above the instruments of their trouble, to God, well knowing that their worst enemies have no power against them, but what is permitted from above.

In afflictions, we must not seek relief by any sinful compliance; but should continually meditate on the truth, purity, and knowledge of our heart-searching God. Hearts sins and secret sins are known to God, and must be reckoned for. He knows the secret of the heart, therefore judges of the words and actions. While our troubles do not drive us from our duty to God, we should not suffer them to drive us from our comfort in God. Let us take care that prosperity and ease do not render us careless and lukewarm. The church of God cannot be prevailed on by persecution to forget God; the believer's heart does not turn back from God. The Spirit of prophecy had reference to those who suffered unto death, for the testimony of Christ. Observe the pleas used, ver. #(25, 26). Not their own merit and righteousness, but the poor sinner's pleas. None that belong to Christ shall be cast off, but every one of them shall be saved, and that for ever. The mercy of God, purchased, promised, and constantly flowing forth, and offered to believers, does away every doubt arising from our sins; while we pray in faith, Redeem us for thy mercies' sake.
